about_full.heading: A leader forged in the rubble of Christchurch.
about_full.subheading: Founder of the Student Volunteer Army, international disaster recovery practitioner, and advocate for trusting young people with real responsibility.
about_full.origin_body:
In February 2011, a devastating earthquake struck Christchurch. Sam Johnson was a university student watching his city break apart — and watching thousands of young people being told to stay out of the way. He disagreed. Using Facebook, he called on students to grab shovels and help dig the city out of liquefaction silt.

Eleven thousand volunteers answered. The Student Volunteer Army was born — proof that young people, given trust and a practical task, will show up in extraordinary numbers.

In the years since, Sam has carried that lesson into disaster zones in Japan, the Philippines, Vanuatu and Nepal, and into classrooms, boardrooms and parliaments across the Pacific, Saudi Arabia and Brazil. His work has been recognised with the Young New Zealander of the Year award, Communicator of the Year, and the Sir Peter Blake Leadership Award.

His vision remains the same as it was in 2011: to catalyse a revolution in youth leadership.
about_full.quote: Young people aren't the leaders of tomorrow. Given a shovel and some trust, they are the leaders of right now.

timeline.title: Student Volunteer Army founded
timeline.description: After the February earthquake, Sam mobilised students through social media to clear liquefaction silt across the city. What began as one Facebook event became a coordinated volunteer force.

timeline.title: Tōhoku earthquake response
timeline.description: Sam joined recovery efforts following the Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami, beginning the international chapter of the SVA model.

timeline.title: Typhoon Haiyan recovery
timeline.description: Supporting community-led recovery after one of the strongest storms ever recorded, applying volunteer coordination lessons from Christchurch.

timeline.title: Cyclone Pam & Nepal earthquake responses
timeline.description: Back-to-back deployments supporting volunteer mobilisation and community resilience in two major disasters.

timeline.title: Global youth leadership advocacy
timeline.description: Sam's work expanded to influencing school students, boardrooms and politicians internationally — championing practical, commonsense youth leadership.

timeline.title: The mission continues
timeline.description: Speaking, advising and building programmes that put young people at the centre of civic life and disaster resilience.

about_teaser.heading: From a student with a shovel to a global voice for young leaders.
about_teaser.body: When the Christchurch earthquakes struck, Sam Johnson mobilised 11,000 students through social media to dig the city out — and the Student Volunteer Army was born. Since then his work has taken him from disaster zones in Japan, the Philippines, Vanuatu and Nepal to boardrooms and parliaments across the Pacific, Saudi Arabia and Brazil.

about.values_heading: Three beliefs that shape the work.

values.title: Practical leadership
values.body: Leadership is a shovel, not a slogan. The fastest way to grow leaders is to give them something real to do and the trust to do it.

values.title: Community first
values.body: Recovery, resilience and change all start with neighbours helping neighbours. Institutions work best when they back communities, not bypass them.

values.title: Young people now
values.body: Young people are not a future asset to be developed — they are a present force to be mobilised, in disasters and in everyday civic life.

projects.title: Student Volunteer Army
projects.description: When the Christchurch earthquakes struck, Sam used Facebook to mobilise students into a coordinated volunteer force, clearing thousands of tonnes of liquefaction silt from the city's streets and homes. The SVA has since grown into a national movement with school, tertiary and community programmes that put young people at the heart of civic service.
